public_rationale: The rat-paper example is established: the authors disclosed Midjourney use, and Frontiers retracted the paper on February 16. An accessible March 17 account also reproduces the lithium paper's chatbot-style opening. However, the original lithium paper was inaccessible through the required reader, and the retrieved corroboration did not independently establish its text by March 14. The combined claim remains unresolved under the specified evidence rules. This is an access and historical-version gap, not evidence that Marcus was wrong.
limitations: The factual examples are strongly corroborated, but only the rat example was verified within the target period.
Several promising sources could not be read or returned unrelated content.
The assessment does not test the subjective ranking expressed by 'clearest'.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In 2024 so far, a now-retracted paper with an AI-generated rat image and a lithium battery paper with an LLM-written opening sentence are the clearest examples of GenAI contaminating science.

statement.excerpt: Two clearest examples so far this year, are the now retracted paper with the above-mentioned rat and a new lithium battery paper, with an opening sentence clearly written by an LLM.
statement.document_title: The Year of the Big-Balled Rat

from_speaker: Two clearest examples so far this year
the now retracted paper with the above-mentioned rat
an opening sentence clearly written by an LLM
our_interpretation: Assess the two factual examples together: an AI-illustrated rat paper already retracted by March 14, and a publicly available lithium-battery paper whose introduction contained unmistakable chatbot-response wording.
'Clearest' expresses the speaker's assessment of the examples; no objective ranking among all scientific publications is supplied.
'Opening sentence' is read as the opening of the introduction, rather than the abstract.
The stated period is January 1 through March 14, 2024.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable records establish both that the rat paper contained AI-generated imagery and had been retracted by the post date, and that the lithium-battery paper already contained the described LLM-style opening by that date.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that either factual example was materially misdescribed: the rat paper lacked AI imagery or was not yet retracted, or the lithium paper lacked the alleged opening during the target period.

evidence.excerpt: This retraction was approved by the Chief Executive Editor of Frontiers.
evidence.locator: Page 1, final paragraph; publication date at top of page
evidence.explanation: The notice identifies the Guo, Dong and Hao paper and dates its retraction to February 16. Its preceding paragraph connects the action to concerns about AI-generated figures and inadequate scientific rigor.

evidence.locator: Page 3, disclosure referring to Figure 1; Figure 1 caption on page 4
evidence.publisher: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology; Xinyu Guo, Liang Dong and Dingjun Hao
evidence.explanation: The original paper discloses Midjourney-generated images and identifies Figure 1 as illustrating cells from rat testes. This establishes the AI provenance of the rat-paper example.

evidence.locator: Paragraph identifying the lithium-metal-anode battery paper
evidence.explanation: This dated account corroborates the alleged opening and identifies the battery paper. Its observation falls three days after the target period, so it is not decisive evidence of the version available by March 14.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A readable original or archived lithium-paper version, or a reliably dated contemporaneous reproduction, showing the introductory boilerplate publicly available by March 14, 2024 would complete the supporting evidence.
